question: What kind of knowing is present even in cognition that follows pervasion?
premises: Some cognition appears to be preceded by manifestation following pervasion.
The preceding argument has undermined a merely sequential account of such cognition.
The author offers a positive characterization of that cognition.
inference: Even cognition that follows pervasion is, at its core, a non-sequential knowing akin to direct perception.
plain_english: Therefore, even the cognition that seems to be preceded by a manifestation following pervasion is, in that very case, a non-sequential knowing of a directly perceptual kind.
